title: Momentum Builds: SmartAgri UGM Strengthens Research-to-Industry Ties on Day Two of INAGRITECH 2026
subtitle: Building on a strong opening, SmartAgri UGM's second day at INAGRITECH 2026 mixed live demos, senior guests, and new collaboration talks at booth A2K4-04.
excerpt: On the second day of INAGRITECH 2026 (July 28–30, JIExpo Kemayoran, Jakarta), the Smart Agriculture Research Center of Universitas Gadjah Mada carried its opening-day momentum forward as booth A2K4-04 stayed busy with hands-on demos of UAV mapping and field sensors, deeper technical conversations, and visits from senior guests and prospective partners.
author: SmartAgri UGM Newsroom
body:
**Jakarta, July 29, 2026.** The Smart Agriculture Research Center (SmartAgri) of Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM) carried its opening-day momentum into the second day of INAGRITECH 2026, Indonesia's largest agricultural technology exhibition, at JIExpo Kemayoran, Jakarta. Booth A2K4-04 stayed busy from the morning onward, as a steady flow of visitors returned for a closer look at the center's precision-agriculture research.

If the first day was about first impressions, the second was about depth. Casual booth visits turned into hands-on demonstrations and detailed conversations about how smart farming tools actually work in the field, from Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imaging and multispectral mapping to sensor-based crop monitoring and data-driven decision-making.

## Deeper Conversations, Hands-On Demos

Much of the day's interest centered on SmartAgri's remote-sensing work. Team members walked visitors through UAV and multispectral field maps, showing how aerial imagery can reveal crop stress, guide water and fertilizer use, and turn an entire field into actionable data. Others gathered around the booth table for a hands-on look at the sensing instruments the team develops and uses in its research.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/inagritech-2026-day2-2.webp) ![](/brand/uploads/notes/inagritech-2026-day2-5.webp)

_SmartAgri UGM researchers walk visitors through UAV and multispectral field maps and demonstrate a field sensor up close. Photo: SmartAgri UGM._

The questions grew more specific as the day went on, a sign that visitors were not only curious about the technology but were weighing how it might fit their own operations, from smallholder plots to industrial-scale farming.

## New Faces, a Wider Network

The second day also widened SmartAgri's circle of contacts. Among the guests were senior figures from academia and industry who stopped by to learn about the center's work, alongside students, practitioners, and prospective partners. Several of these conversations opened the door to potential collaboration on developing and applying agricultural technology in Indonesia.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/inagritech-2026-day2-1.webp) ![](/brand/uploads/notes/inagritech-2026-day2-3.webp)

_A senior guest visits the SmartAgri UGM booth, while conversations with visitors continue at a steady pace throughout the day. Photo: SmartAgri UGM._

For the SmartAgri team, these exchanges are the real value of the exhibition: a chance to see how campus research resonates with the people who would ultimately use it, and to bring the journey from laboratory to field a step closer. INAGRITECH 2026 runs through July 30, 2026, and the SmartAgri booth remains open to visitors interested in its research and collaboration opportunities.

> [!ABOUT] About SmartAgri UGM
>
> The Smart Agriculture Research Center (SmartAgri) is a research center under the Department of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering, Faculty of Agricultural Technology, Universitas Gadjah Mada. It focuses on precision agriculture, _controlled-environment farming_, remote sensing (UAV and hyperspectral imaging), greenhouse automation, and agro-informatics to advance smart and sustainable agriculture in Indonesia.
